```{r}
library(arrow)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)


if (file.exists("data/daily.rds")) {
  daily <- readRDS("data/daily.rds")
  message("Loaded daily.rds, skipping scan.")
} else {

  pq <- list.files("cache", pattern = "\\.parquet$", full.names = TRUE)
  dir.create("cache_daily", showWarnings = FALSE)
  chunks <- split(pq, ceiling(seq_along(pq) / 10))   # 10 files per chunk

  t0 <- Sys.time()
  for (k in seq_along(chunks)) {
    out <- sprintf("cache_daily/daily_%03d.rds", k)
    if (!file.exists(out)) {
      chunk_ds <- open_dataset(chunks[[k]])

      # Exclude 10001_20000 (uses source_file if present in cache, else CUSTOMER_NUMBER)
      if ("source_file" %in% names(chunk_ds)) {
        chunk_ds <- chunk_ds |>
          filter(!grepl("2026 Avangrid Hackathon Data_10001_20000", source_file, fixed = TRUE))
      } else {
        chunk_ds <- chunk_ds |>
          filter(as.numeric(CUSTOMER_NUMBER) <= 10000)
      }

      res <- chunk_ds |>
        filter(is_complete_hour == "1") |>
        mutate(kwh = as.numeric(hourly_kwh)) |>
        group_by(usage_date) |>
        summarise(total_kwh = sum(kwh, na.rm = TRUE), n_rows = n()) |>
        collect()
      saveRDS(res, out)
    }
    el <- as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), t0, units = "mins"))
    cat(sprintf("[%s] chunk %d/%d (%.0f%%) | %.1f min elapsed\n",
                format(Sys.time(), "%H:%M:%S"), k, length(chunks),
                100 * k / length(chunks), el))
    flush.console()
  }

  daily <- list.files("cache_daily", pattern = "\\.rds$", full.names = TRUE) |>
    lapply(readRDS) |>
    bind_rows() |>
    group_by(usage_date) |>
    summarise(total_kwh = sum(total_kwh), n_rows = sum(n_rows)) |>
    mutate(
      date = as.Date(usage_date),
      avg_kwh_per_customer_hour = total_kwh / n_rows,
      approx_customers = n_rows / 24
    ) |>
    arrange(date)

  dir.create("data", showWarnings = FALSE)
  saveRDS(daily, "data/daily.rds")
}

sum(is.na(daily$date))        # want 0
range(daily$date)             # want 2025-09-01 to about 2026-08-31
nrow(daily)                   # want ~365
daily |> arrange(n_rows) |> head(10)

# Total daily usage
p1 <- ggplot(daily, aes(date, total_kwh)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(title = "Total daily kWh, all customers", x = NULL, y = "kWh") +
  theme_minimal()

# Average per customer-hour (fair if customer count changes)
p2 <- ggplot(daily, aes(date, avg_kwh_per_customer_hour)) +
  geom_col(fill = "darkorange") +
  labs(title = "Average kWh per customer-hour, by day", x = NULL, y = "kWh") +
  theme_minimal()

# Monthly bars (cleaner for a full year)
monthly <- daily |>
  mutate(month = as.Date(format(date, "%Y-%m-01"))) |>
  group_by(month) |>
  summarise(total_kwh = sum(total_kwh), n_rows = sum(n_rows), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(avg_kwh = total_kwh / n_rows)

p3 <- ggplot(monthly, aes(month, avg_kwh)) +
  geom_col(fill = "seagreen") +
  scale_x_date(date_labels = "%b %Y", date_breaks = "1 month") +
  labs(title = "Average kWh per customer-hour, by month", x = NULL, y = "kWh") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

# Customers reporting per day (coverage check)
p4 <- ggplot(daily, aes(date, approx_customers)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(title = "Approx. customers reporting per day", x = NULL, y = "Customers") +
  theme_minimal()

p1; p2; p3; p4
```

```{r}
library(arrow)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(cli)
library(cluster)
library(ggplot2)

# ==================================================================
# Design
#   * Never collect the raw 200M rows. Arrow scans the dataset, filters,
#     casts and aggregates; only small summary tables come into R.
#   * Work month by month. Each month is reduced to MERGEABLE aggregates
#     (sum, count, max) per customer x day type x hour, and written to a
#     parquet checkpoint. Means are rebuilt later as sum / n, so the
#     result is exactly what a single big group_by would give.
#   * Progress bar with ETA, a log file you can `tail -f`, and resume:
#     months already checkpointed are skipped if the script is re-run.
#
# Assumes `ds` is an Arrow Dataset: ds <- open_dataset("path/to/data")
# ==================================================================

ckpt_dir <- "ckpt_shape"
dir.create(file.path(ckpt_dir, "profile"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
log_file <- file.path(ckpt_dir, "progress.log")

log_msg <- function(...) {
  line <- sprintf("[%s] %s", format(Sys.time(), "%H:%M:%S"), sprintf(...))
  cat(line, "\n", file = log_file, append = TRUE)
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 0. Sanity check the chr columns once, on a small slice (cheap)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
pq <- list.files("cache_clean", pattern = "\\.parquet$", full.names = TRUE)
ds <- open_dataset(pq, format = "parquet")


ds |> head(1e5) |> collect() |> count(is_complete_hour, day_type)
# Adjust the accepted values in `complete_vals` below if yours differ.
complete_vals <- c("TRUE", "T", "1", "Y", "YES")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. List the months to process (reads one column only)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
months <- ds |>
  transmute(ym = substr(usage_date, 1, 7)) |>
  distinct() |>
  collect() |>
  pull(ym) |>
  sort()
cat("Months to process:", length(months), "\n")

season_of <- function(ym) {
  m <- as.integer(substr(ym, 6, 7))
  c("winter", "winter", "spring", "spring", "spring", "summer",
    "summer", "summer", "fall", "fall", "fall", "winter")[m]
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Aggregate one month inside Arrow, write checkpoint
#    Output grain: customer x day_type x hour (tiny vs the raw data)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
aggregate_month <- function(ym) {
  lo <- paste0(ym, "-01")   # usage_date is ISO text, so string range
  hi <- paste0(ym, "-31")   # comparison works and lets Arrow prune files

  out <- ds |>
    filter(usage_date >= lo, usage_date <= hi) |>
    filter(toupper(is_complete_hour) %in% complete_vals) |>
    transmute(
      CUSTOMER_NUMBER,
      hour_ending,
      dt  = if_else(day_type == "Weekday", "wd", "we"),
      kwh = as.numeric(hourly_kwh)
    ) |>
    filter(!is.na(kwh), kwh >= 0) |>
    group_by(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, dt, hour_ending) |>
    summarise(
      sum_kwh = sum(kwh),
      n       = n(),
      max_kwh = max(kwh),
      hrs_gt5 = sum(if_else(kwh > 5, 1L, 0L))   # hours above 5 kW
    ) |>
    collect() |>
    mutate(season = season_of(ym), ym = ym)

  write_parquet(out, file.path(ckpt_dir, "profile", paste0(ym, ".parquet")))
  invisible(sum(out$n))
}

# Time one month first to estimate total runtime:
system.time(aggregate_month(months[1]))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Main loop with progress bar, ETA and resume
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
rows_done <- 0
t0 <- Sys.time()
cli_progress_bar(
  "Aggregating",
  total  = length(months),
  format = paste0("{pb_spin} {pb_bar} {pb_percent} | {pb_current}/{pb_total} months",
                  " | ETA {pb_eta} | {pb_status}")
)

for (ym in months) {
  f <- file.path(ckpt_dir, "profile", paste0(ym, ".parquet"))
  if (file.exists(f)) {
    n_rows <- sum(as.numeric(read_parquet(f, col_select = "n")$n))
    log_msg("%s skipped (checkpoint exists)", ym)
  } else {
    tm <- system.time(n_rows <- aggregate_month(ym))[["elapsed"]]
    log_msg("%s done: %.1fM rows in %.0fs", ym, n_rows / 1e6, tm)
  }
  rows_done <- rows_done + n_rows
  cli_progress_update(
    status = sprintf("%s | %.1fM complete-hour rows", ym, rows_done / 1e6)
  )
}
cli_progress_done()
cat("Aggregation finished in",
    format(round(difftime(Sys.time(), t0, units = "mins"), 1)), "\n")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Merge checkpoints (small: customers x ~48 hours x months)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Merge checkpoints (small: customers x ~48 hours x months)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
prof <- open_dataset(file.path(ckpt_dir, "profile")) |>
  group_by(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, season, dt, hour_ending) |>
  summarise(
    sum_kwh = sum(sum_kwh),
    n       = sum(n),
    max_kwh = max(max_kwh),
    hrs_gt5 = sum(hrs_gt5)
  ) |>
  collect() |>
  ungroup()   # collect() keeps the leftover grouping (customer, season, dt);
              # that grouping breaks pivot_wider below, so drop it here
 
cat("Profile rows:", nrow(prof), " Customers:", n_distinct(prof$CUSTOMER_NUMBER), "\n")
 
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Keep customer-seasons with enough data, then build shape vectors
#    shape = (mean kWh in this hour/day type) / (customer's season mean)
#    1.0 = an average hour for that home, so size drops out.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
min_hours <- 14 * 24

season_stats <- prof |>
  group_by(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, season) |>
  summarise(season_hours = sum(n), season_sum = sum(sum_kwh), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(season_hours >= min_hours, season_sum > 0) |>
  mutate(season_mean = season_sum / season_hours)

shape_wide <- prof |>
  inner_join(season_stats, by = c("CUSTOMER_NUMBER", "season")) |>
  mutate(
    shape = (sum_kwh / n) / season_mean,
    feat  = sprintf("%s_%s_h%02d", season, dt, hour_ending)
  ) |>
  select(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, feat, shape) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = feat, values_from = shape) |>
  drop_na()

ids <- shape_wide$CUSTOMER_NUMBER
X   <- as.matrix(shape_wide[, -1])
rownames(X) <- ids
cat("Clustering", nrow(X), "customers on", ncol(X), "features\n")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. PCA (no scaling: features already share a unitless scale)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
pca  <- prcomp(X, center = TRUE, scale. = FALSE)
n_pc <- which(cumsum(pca$sdev^2) / sum(pca$sdev^2) >= 0.90)[1]
Z    <- pca$x[, 1:n_pc, drop = FALSE]
cat("Using", n_pc, "PCs (90% variance)\n")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Choose k (silhouette on a sample, since it is O(n^2))
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
set.seed(42)
samp   <- sample(nrow(Z), min(3000, nrow(Z)))
d_samp <- dist(Z[samp, , drop = FALSE])

ks <- 2:10
eval_k <- lapply(ks, function(k) {
  km  <- kmeans(Z, centers = k, nstart = 10, iter.max = 100)
  sil <- silhouette(km$cluster[samp], d_samp)
  log_msg("k=%d silhouette=%.3f", k, mean(sil[, 3]))
  tibble(k = k, tot_withinss = km$tot.withinss, sil = mean(sil[, 3]))
}) |> bind_rows()

print(eval_k)
ggplot(eval_k, aes(k, sil)) + geom_line() + geom_point() + labs(title = "Average silhouette")
ggplot(eval_k, aes(k, tot_withinss)) + geom_line() + geom_point() + labs(title = "Elbow")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. Final clustering
#    For millions of customers, ClusterR::MiniBatchKmeans is a drop-in
#    faster option. Plain kmeans is fine for tens/hundreds of thousands.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
k_final <- 6
set.seed(42)
km <- kmeans(Z, centers = k_final, nstart = 25, iter.max = 100)
assign <- tibble(CUSTOMER_NUMBER = ids, cluster = factor(km$cluster))
print(assign |> count(cluster) |> mutate(pct = round(n / sum(n), 3)))

# Cross-check with Ward hierarchical on a sample (full dist matrix would
# not fit in memory at this scale)
hc_idx <- sample(nrow(Z), min(5000, nrow(Z)))
hc     <- hclust(dist(Z[hc_idx, , drop = FALSE]), method = "ward.D2")
print(table(kmeans = km$cluster[hc_idx], ward = cutree(hc, k = k_final)))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 9. Plot centroid shapes, computed from the aggregates (no raw data)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
shape_long <- prof |>
  inner_join(season_stats, by = c("CUSTOMER_NUMBER", "season")) |>
  mutate(shape = (sum_kwh / n) / season_mean) |>
  inner_join(assign, by = "CUSTOMER_NUMBER")

shape_long |>
  group_by(cluster, season, dt, hour_ending) |>
  summarise(mean_shape = mean(shape),
            lo = quantile(shape, 0.25),
            hi = quantile(shape, 0.75), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(hour_ending, mean_shape)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_grid(cluster ~ season + dt) +
  labs(y = "Load relative to customer's mean (1 = average hour)",
       title = "Cluster centroid shapes (line) with IQR (band)")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 10. Volume and BESS-relevant metrics (exact, from the same aggregates)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
volume <- prof |>
  group_by(CUSTOMER_NUMBER) |>
  summarise(
    mean_kw        = sum(sum_kwh) / sum(n),
    peak_kw        = max(max_kwh),
    load_factor    = mean_kw / peak_kw,
    sys_peak_share = sum(sum_kwh[hour_ending %in% 17:20]) / sum(sum_kwh),
    pct_hrs_gt5kw  = sum(hrs_gt5) / sum(n),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

cluster_profile <- assign |>
  left_join(volume, by = "CUSTOMER_NUMBER") |>
  group_by(cluster) |>
  summarise(n = n(),
            across(c(mean_kw, peak_kw, load_factor, sys_peak_share, pct_hrs_gt5kw), median),
            .groups = "drop")
print(cluster_profile)

# Save results
saveRDS(list(assign = assign, volume = volume, pca = pca, km = km,
             cluster_profile = cluster_profile),
        file.path(ckpt_dir, "shape_clustering_results.rds"))
```


```{r}

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

# ==================================================================
# Run AFTER shape_clustering_large.R, in the same R session. Uses these
# objects it created: shape_long, season_stats, assign, cluster_profile.
# (shape_long is only built in section 9 of that script; re-run that
#  block if it is missing.)
#
# hour_ending = the hour that ENDS at that time, so 17 = 4pm-5pm.
# ==================================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Centroids: mean normalized shape per cluster x season x day type
#    (1.0 = the customer's own average hour)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
cent <- shape_long |>
  group_by(cluster, season, dt, hour_ending) |>
  summarise(shape = mean(shape), .groups = "drop")

cent_avg <- cent |>                      # averaged over seasons
  group_by(cluster, dt, hour_ending) |>
  summarise(shape = mean(shape), .groups = "drop")

# Cluster labels that include size, e.g. "3 (n=4,382, 14%)"
sizes <- assign |> count(cluster) |> mutate(pct = n / sum(n))
lab   <- setNames(sprintf("Cluster %s (n=%s, %.0f%%)", sizes$cluster,
                          format(sizes$n, big.mark = ","), 100 * sizes$pct),
                  sizes$cluster)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Plots
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# (a) Overall daily shape, weekday vs weekend
p_overall <- ggplot(cent_avg, aes(hour_ending, shape, colour = dt)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(16.5, 20.5), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
  facet_wrap(~cluster, labeller = labeller(cluster = lab)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(wd = "#1f77b4", we = "#ff7f0e"),
                      labels = c(wd = "Weekday", we = "Weekend"), name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 24, 6)) +
  labs(x = "Hour ending", y = "Load relative to own average (1 = average hour)",
       title = "Cluster centroid shapes",
       subtitle = "Dashed lines mark the 4-8pm system peak window") +
  theme_minimal()
print(p_overall)

# (b) Weekday shape by season: shows heating / cooling / seasonal behavior
p_season <- cent |>
  filter(dt == "wd") |>
  ggplot(aes(hour_ending, shape, colour = season)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~cluster, labeller = labeller(cluster = lab)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 24, 6)) +
  labs(x = "Hour ending", y = "Relative load", title = "Weekday centroids by season") +
  theme_minimal()
print(p_season)

ggsave("centroids_overall.png", p_overall, width = 11, height = 7, dpi = 200)
ggsave("centroids_season.png",  p_season,  width = 11, height = 7, dpi = 200)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Numbers behind the shapes (cluster-level descriptors)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
time_window <- function(h) case_when(
  h %in% 7:9   ~ "morning",    # 6am-9am
  h %in% 10:16 ~ "midday",     # 9am-4pm
  h %in% 17:21 ~ "evening",    # 4pm-9pm
  TRUE         ~ "overnight"   # 9pm-6am
)

# Peak hour and peak-to-trough ratio
peaks <- cent_avg |>
  group_by(cluster, dt) |>
  summarise(peak_hr = hour_ending[which.max(shape)],
            peak_ratio = max(shape) / min(shape), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = dt, values_from = c(peak_hr, peak_ratio))

# Share of daily energy in each window
shares <- cent_avg |>
  mutate(win = time_window(hour_ending)) |>
  group_by(cluster, dt) |>
  mutate(tot = sum(shape)) |>
  group_by(cluster, dt, win) |>
  summarise(share = sum(shape) / first(tot), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = c(win, dt), values_from = share,
              names_glue = "{win}_share_{dt}")

# Weekday vs weekend similarity (low = routine differs on weekends)
wdwe <- cent_avg |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = dt, values_from = shape) |>
  group_by(cluster) |>
  summarise(wd_we_cor = cor(wd, we), .groups = "drop")

# Seasonal level: median season mean kW, winter vs summer
seas <- season_stats |>
  inner_join(assign, by = "CUSTOMER_NUMBER") |>
  group_by(cluster, season) |>
  summarise(m = median(season_mean), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = season, values_from = m)

seas$winter_summer <- if (all(c("winter", "summer") %in% names(seas))) {
  seas$winter / seas$summer
} else NA_real_

desc <- cluster_profile |>
  left_join(peaks,  by = "cluster") |>
  left_join(shares, by = "cluster") |>
  left_join(wdwe,   by = "cluster") |>
  left_join(select(seas, cluster, any_of(c("winter", "summer")), winter_summer),
            by = "cluster")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. DRAFT one-line labels from transparent rules
#    The clusters look alike in volume, so thresholds are RELATIVE
#    (compared with the other clusters). Edit these after looking at
#    the plots; treat the output as a starting point, not a finding.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
desc <- desc |>
  mutate(
    when = case_when(
      peak_hr_wd %in% 6:9    ~ "morning-peaking",
      peak_hr_wd %in% 10:16  ~ "midday-peaking",
      peak_hr_wd %in% 17:22  ~ "evening-peaking",
      TRUE                   ~ "overnight-peaking"
    ),
    spiky     = if_else(peak_ratio_wd >= quantile(peak_ratio_wd, 2/3), "spiky", NA_character_),
    flat      = if_else(peak_ratio_wd <= quantile(peak_ratio_wd, 1/3), "flat",  NA_character_),
    weekend   = if_else(wd_we_cor    <= quantile(wd_we_cor, 1/3), "weekend routine differs", NA_character_),
    wfh       = if_else(midday_share_wd >= quantile(midday_share_wd, 2/3), "high daytime use", NA_character_),
    season_tag = case_when(
      is.na(winter_summer)   ~ NA_character_,
      winter_summer >= 1.15  ~ "winter-heavy",
      winter_summer <= 0.87  ~ "summer-heavy",
      TRUE                   ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(draft_label = paste(na.omit(c(when, spiky, flat, wfh, weekend, season_tag)),
                             collapse = ", ")) |>
  ungroup()

# Readable summary table
desc |>
  transmute(
    cluster, n,
    peak_weekday   = sprintf("%d:00-%d:00", peak_hr_wd - 1, peak_hr_wd),
    peak_ratio_wd  = round(peak_ratio_wd, 2),
    evening_share  = round(evening_share_wd, 3),
    midday_share   = round(midday_share_wd, 3),
    overnight_share = round(overnight_share_wd, 3),
    wd_we_cor      = round(wd_we_cor, 3),
    winter_summer  = round(winter_summer, 2),
    sys_peak_share = round(sys_peak_share, 3),
    pct_hrs_gt5kw  = round(pct_hrs_gt5kw, 3),
    draft_label
  ) |>
  print(width = Inf)

# Save for the write-up
saveRDS(desc, file.path(ckpt_dir, "cluster_descriptions.rds"))

```
